claims.text: Introducing a controlled nano-oxide dispersion into a refractory high-entropy alloy improves its mechanical performance.
Y2O3 can function as a stable nano-oxide dispersoid in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Nano-oxide particles impede dislocation motion in the alloy matrix.
Nano-oxide particles act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Impeded dislocation motion increases alloy strength.
Impeded dislocation motion improves creep resistance.
Defect-sink activity of nano-oxides preserves microstructural stability during irradiation.
The processing intervention can produce a uniformly dispersed, fine-scale population of nano-oxide particles in the matrix.
The nano-oxide-dispersed alloy will have higher yield strength than an otherwise comparable alloy without engineered oxide dispersoids.
The nano-oxide-dispersed alloy will have better creep resistance than an otherwise comparable alloy without engineered oxide dispersoids.
The nano-oxide-dispersed alloy will retain thermal stability comparable to the baseline alloy.
The nano-oxide-dispersed alloy will retain irradiation stability comparable to the baseline alloy.
The proposed benefits are expected to persist at temperatures above 800 degrees Celsius.
The proposed benefits are expected under irradiation exposures representative of nuclear or space environments.
Coarsening of the nano-oxide particles can compromise the performance benefits.
Agglomeration of the nano-oxide particles can compromise the performance benefits.
Adverse interactions between oxide particles and the alloy matrix can compromise the performance benefits.
The magnitude of mechanical improvement depends on processing parameters and exposure conditions.
